original_question: Prove that any generalized minimal flow admits a background region B0 on which the vorticity is constant, with the remaining vorticity organized into blob regions separated from that background.
target_in_paper: §6.3, Problem 15, with notation and scope supplied by Definition 6.7 and the immediately preceding blob/background discussion. The draft’s phrases “background region B0” and “blob regions” match the passage “The flow domain M contains some number of vorticity blobs B1, . . . , BN and a background B0,” followed by “Problem 15. For any GM-flow curl u = const in B0.” ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the intended object (a generalized minimal flow / GM-flow), the distinguished background region B0, and the asserted conclusion that the vorticity is constant there. It also reflects the motivating numerical picture of blob regions against a background, which is exactly the context used to introduce Problem 15. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s ambient setting here is a compact analytic Riemannian 2-manifold M, with or without boundary, not an arbitrary flow domain. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

A GM-flow must be defined via Definition 6.7: u lies in the Yudovich space YU(M) of divergence-free vector fields with curl u in L∞(M), and for every w in the weak H^1-closure of its Euler orbit one has ||curl w||L2 = ||curl u||L2. Without this, the question is not stand-alone. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
The official formulation is an open problem/conjectural statement (Problem 15), not a proved theorem. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The paper does not formally define the blob regions B1,...,BN or the background region B0 beyond the surrounding numerical description, so a faithful rewrite should treat that decomposition as the paper’s motivating picture rather than as a new fully axiomatized hypothesis. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

Your draft adds more than the official statement by asserting that the remaining vorticity is “organized into blob regions separated from that background.” The paper mentions blobs only as contextual numerical evidence and does not separately formalize or ask to prove a separation theorem. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
The notation should match the paper: “GM-flow” and the conclusion “curl u = const in B0.” ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

Problem 14 is a nearby but different claim: it asks that vorticity level lines of a GM-flow be real-analytic. A faithful rewrite of your draft should not merge that analyticity problem into Problem 15 unless explicitly stated. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

Because §6.3 moves between a Yudovich state u and a time-evolving GM-flow u(x,t), a self-contained rewrite should fix the GM notion through Definition 6.7 and then state the background-vorticity claim for that GM-flow/state. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
refined_question: Let M be a compact analytic Riemannian 2-manifold, with or without boundary, and let YU(M) be the Yudovich space of divergence-free vector fields u on M such that curl u is in L∞(M). Let O(u) be the Euler orbit of u and Obar(u) its weak H^1-closure. If u in YU(M) is a generalized minimal flow in the sense of Definition 6.7, namely ||curl w||L2 = ||curl u||L2 for every w in Obar(u), then, in the blob/background picture described in §6.3 (where the domain is viewed as consisting of vorticity blobs B1,...,BN and a background region B0), prove that the vorticity is constant on the background region; equivalently, prove that curl u = c on B0 for some constant c. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets §6.3 rather than any statement in the paper’s opening section, because only §6.3 uses the specific language of GM-flows, vorticity blobs, and a background region B0. Among the nearby official statements, Problem 15 is the exact match; Definition 6.7 provides the hidden definition of GM-flow, while Problem 14 is a neighboring but distinct analyticity question. The refined version therefore imports Definition 6.7 to make the question self-contained, keeps the blob/background terminology only to the extent the paper itself uses it, and avoids broadening the target into a stronger decomposition-or-separation theorem that the paper does not formally state. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
